title: Settings
description: Request handling, access and maintenance for this proxy. Each card saves on its own.
discardBody: Some settings cards have changes that are not saved. Leaving this page discards them.
allowOverUsageHint: Accounts keep serving requests after their credits run out.
usageRefresh.title: Background usage refresh
usageRefresh.hint: How often the proxy checks every account's credits and renews tokens that are about to expire. When off, usage updates only when you refresh an account.
lenientStreamIntegrityHint: Kiro marks a turn complete with a stop reason or a metering event. Some IdC and Enterprise accounts send neither, so their replies are rejected as truncated.
lenientStreamIntegrityRisk: Only for affected accounts: a cut-off reply can pass as complete.
routingMode.title: Routing mode
routingMode.weightedHint: New requests rotate across the enabled accounts. An account with weight 2 gets about twice as many as an account with weight 1.
routingMode.priorityHint: New requests go to the account with the lowest priority number. If that account is cooling down, out of credits, disabled or does not serve the model, the next one takes over.
routingMode.priorityMore: Set each account's priority in its details. Accounts with the same number follow the list order. Ongoing conversations follow the priority too: as soon as a higher-priority account is free again, the next turn goes to it. Among accounts with the same priority, Keep conversations on one account keeps each conversation where it is.
rpmLimitHint: An account that started this many requests in the last minute is skipped until its count drops below the limit. When every account is at the limit, new requests get a 429 error.
rpmLimitMore: Off by default. A retry on the same account does not count again, but a retry on another account counts for that account. The Accounts page shows each account's requests in the last minute and today.
rpmLimitInvalid: Requests per minute must be a whole number between 1 and {max}.
sessionAffinityHint: Follow-up turns go back to the account that answered the previous turn, which already holds the prompt cache. Turn this off to pick the account for every request by the routing mode.
sessionAffinityMore: New conversations are still routed by the routing mode. If that account is cooling down, out of credits or failing, the request moves to another account. In priority mode, it also moves when an account with a higher priority is free.
selfHeal.enable: Bring back accounts the proxy blocked
selfHeal.hint: When no account can serve requests, the proxy lifts the blocks it set itself after sign-in failures or repeated errors, then tries again.
selfHeal.more: Accounts suspended by Kiro, accounts you turned off and accounts waiting for their credits to reset are never touched. An account that fails again after a heal is blocked again.
selfHeal.intervalInvalid: Enter a whole number of seconds from {min} to {max}.
selfHeal.rounds: Maximum heals without a successful request
selfHeal.roundsHint: From 0 to {max}. 0 means no limit. After this many heals, the proxy stops healing until a request succeeds or you resume it.
selfHeal.roundsInvalid: Enter a whole number from 0 to {max}.
selfHeal.never: The proxy has not needed to heal any account yet.
selfHeal.roundsUsed: {used} of {max} heals used since the last successful request.
selfHeal.roundsUsedUnlimited_one: {count} heal since the last successful request (no limit).
selfHeal.roundsUsedUnlimited_other: {count} heals since the last successful request (no limit).
selfHeal.halted: Self-heal stopped after reaching its limit without a successful request. Check the accounts, then resume.
selfHeal.toastHealed_one: Self-heal brought {count} account back into rotation.
selfHeal.toastHealed_other: Self-heal brought {count} accounts back into rotation.
selfHeal.toastHalted: Self-heal stopped because accounts keep failing after each heal. Check the accounts.
autoContinueEnable: Continue answers cut off by the output limit
autoContinueHint: Kiro stops a single answer at about 8192 output tokens. When an answer stops there without a tool call, the proxy asks Kiro to continue and appends the rest.
autoContinueMore: Usage is summed across requests. Each continuation is another billed upstream request, and the seams can occasionally repeat or skip a few words.
autoContinueMaxHint: Between 1 and 10. Continuation also stops at the client's own {param}.
autoContinueMaxInvalid: Maximum continuations must be a whole number between 1 and {max}.
structuredToolHistory: Send earlier tool calls as structured tool calls
structuredToolHistoryHint: Earlier tool calls and results reach the model as real tool calls, so long agent sessions keep calling tools. Turn this off to always send earlier tool activity as plain text.
structuredToolHistoryMore: A pair falls back to plain text when the request does not declare that tool or the call and result IDs do not match. If Kiro rejects the structured form, the proxy retries once with plain text and keeps using plain text for an hour.
imageResizeEnable: Shrink large images before sending them
imageResizeHint: Kiro rejects very large images, such as full-screen screenshots. An image over either limit below is scaled down, keeping its aspect ratio, before it is sent to Kiro. Smaller images are sent unchanged.
imageResizeMore: A resized image is saved as JPEG at quality 85. A transparent PNG stays a PNG if it fits the size limit; otherwise it gets a white background. An animated GIF keeps only its first frame. An image the proxy cannot read is sent unchanged.
imageResizeMaxDimensionHint: In pixels, between 256 and 4096. Claude scales larger images down to about 1568 pixels anyway.
imageResizeMaxDimensionInvalid: Maximum width or height must be a whole number between {min} and {max}.
imageResizeMaxKBHint: In KB, between 50 and 4096. A larger image is compressed more, then scaled down further if it still does not fit.
imageResizeMaxKBInvalid: Maximum file size must be a whole number between {min} and {max}.
thinkingHint: Choose the model suffix that turns on thinking and how thinking output reaches each API.
thinkingSuffixHint: Add this suffix to a model name to turn on thinking, for example {example}.
modelMappingsHint: Map client model names to Kiro model IDs. Rules run in order, and the first rule whose text appears in the model name wins. A model Kiro already serves is only mapped by a rule with its full name.
modelMappings.resetBody_one: Your {count} mapping is replaced by the {defaults} defaults when you save.
modelMappings.resetBody_other: Your {count} mappings are replaced by the {defaults} defaults when you save.
modelMappings.editorDescription: Requests whose model name contains the text go to the Kiro model instead.
modelMappings.matchHint: Matches when this text appears anywhere in the client's model name, in any case. A model Kiro already serves only matches a rule with its full name. Rules run top to bottom; the first match wins.
modelMappings.targetHint: The Kiro model ID the request uses instead.
modelMappings.resetNote: An empty list is not kept after a restart. The proxy then uses the defaults.
modelMappings.noRules: No model mappings. Direct Claude model IDs still work.
modelMappings.dragInstructions: To pick up a mapping, press Space or Enter. Use the arrow keys to move it, Space or Enter to drop it, and Escape to cancel.
modelMappings.dragCancel: Reordering canceled. Mapping {from} stays in place.
endpointSettingsHint: Choose which Kiro endpoint receives requests.
endpointHint: Automatic picks an endpoint based on availability.
endpointFallbackHint: When off, only the selected endpoint is used.
upstream.title: Upstream domain & region
upstream.hint: Where the proxy sends requests to Kiro. These settings apply to every account from the next request on.
upstream.domainHint: Newer Kiro clients use Kiro (kiro.dev) for chat and web search. Usage and model lists always come from AWS.
upstream.effectiveHost: The Kiro IDE endpoint and web search go to {host}.
upstream.effectiveHostAuto: The Kiro IDE endpoint and web search go to {host}, in each account's own region.
upstream.apiRegionHint: Sends every account's requests to this region. Kiro rejects a request when the region does not match the account's profile.
upstream.authRegionHint: Where Builder ID and IAM Identity Center tokens are refreshed. Leave it empty unless an account's region is wrong.
upstream.authRegionInvalid: Enter an AWS region code, such as us-east-1.
adminPasswordHint: Changing the password ends every other signed-in session. This browser stays signed in.
passwordTooShort: Password must be at least 8 characters.
proxyHint: Send Kiro and sign-in traffic through a SOCKS5, HTTP or HTTPS proxy. Changes apply right away, without a restart.
proxyHintPoolOn: The proxy pool is on, so accounts without their own proxy reach Kiro through the pool. This proxy is used for sign-in, and as the fallback when no pool proxy is healthy.
proxyHostHasPort: Put the port in the Port field, not after the host.
proxyHostInvalid: Enter a host name or IP address with no spaces or slashes.
proxyNoneHint: Connect from this server's own network and IP address.
proxySocks5Hint: Tunnel each connection. Works with SSH tunnels and most VPN apps.
proxyHttpHint: Use HTTP CONNECT, over HTTP or HTTPS. Common on company and cloud networks.
proxyProtocolHint: HTTPS also encrypts the link to the proxy, its password included. The proxy must accept TLS.
proxyPasteTip: Paste a full URL such as {example} to fill every field.
proxyRemoveBody: Kiro and sign-in traffic will leave from this server's own IP address right away.
proxyApplyNote: Saving switches Kiro and sign-in traffic to this proxy right away.
responseHeadersHint: Add your own headers to every API response, including streams and errors. Values can use variables, for example to match NewAPI or OneAPI logs to this proxy's request log.
responseHeaders.timing: Values are filled in when the response starts. A stream starts with its first event, so {account} is the account that streams the answer. A header with an empty value is not sent. If the proxy already sets a header, such as Cache-Control on a stream, the proxy's value is kept.
responseHeaders.empty: No custom headers yet. For example, {example} lets NewAPI or OneAPI match their logs to this proxy's request log.
responseHeaders.limit: You can add up to {max} headers.
responseHeaders.editorDescription: Sent on every response from /v1/messages, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/models and count_tokens.
responseHeaders.name: Header name
responseHeaders.nameHint: Letters, digits and symbols such as - or _, with no spaces. Headers the proxy manages, such as Content-Type, Connection or CORS headers, are not allowed.
responseHeaders.valueHint: Text and variables, on one line, up to {max} bytes.
responseHeaders.var.request_id: A new ID for each request. The request log shows it as Trace ID.
responseHeaders.var.model: The model the client asked for. Empty on /v1/models and when the request body cannot be read.
responseHeaders.var.account_id: The ID of the Kiro account that answers. Empty when no account was called, such as for count_tokens.
responseHeaders.var.key_id: The ID of the client's API key. Empty when API keys are not required.
responseHeaders.var.client_ip: The client's IP address as this server sees it. X-Forwarded-For is not read.
responseHeaders.error.nameInvalid: A header name can only use letters, digits and symbols such as - _ . ~, with no spaces or colons.
responseHeaders.error.nameTooLong: A header name can be at most {max} characters.
responseHeaders.error.nameForbidden: The proxy manages {name}, so it cannot be set here.
responseHeaders.error.valueInvalid: The value cannot contain line breaks or control characters.
responseHeaders.error.valueTooLong: The value can be at most {max} bytes.
serverLog.title: Server log
serverLog.hint: How much the server writes to its own log. A change applies at once and is kept after a restart.
serverLog.more: Debug adds a line for each request and each resized image. Info shows start-up, account and warning lines. The other two levels show only problems.
serverLog.debugWarning: Debug also writes request contents, such as prompts, to the log. Set it back to Info when you are done.
serverLog.envNote: The LOG_LEVEL environment variable is set, so it picks the level again at each start.
promptFilterHint: Clean system prompts before they reach Kiro. Built-in filters run first, then custom rules in list order.
filterClaudeCode: Replace Claude Code CLI system prompts
filterClaudeCodeHint: Detects Claude Code's built-in system prompt and swaps it for a compact backend prompt. The other filters and rules then skip it.
filterEnvNoiseHint: Removes injected environment variables, git status, recent commits and similar noise from system prompts.
customRulesHint: A line filter drops every line that contains its text, in any case. A regex rule replaces each match; {group} inserts a captured group.
promptFilter.name: Rule name
promptFilter.invalidRegex: This regex does not compile; the proxy skips it.
promptFilter.matchHintContains: Every line that contains this text is removed. Case is ignored.
promptFilter.matchHintRegex: A Go (RE2) regular expression. Every match is replaced.
promptFilter.replaceHint: Leave empty to delete the match. {group} inserts a captured group.
logRetentionHint: Request and error log entries older than the number of days below are deleted, so the database stops growing. Overview totals, the model mix and Usage by key still include them.
logRetentionMore: Cleanup runs 2 minutes after the server starts, then once a day, and right after you save. It deletes in small batches, so requests are not slowed down. New entries reuse the freed space, but the database file does not shrink.
logRetentionDaysHint: Between 1 and {max}. The Requests page shows only the entries kept.
logRetentionDaysInvalid: Days must be a whole number between 1 and {max}.
logRetentionNeverRun: No cleanup since the server started
logRetentionArchived_one: {n} deleted request still counted in totals
logRetentionArchived_other: {n} deleted requests still counted in totals
resetStatsHint: Deletes request history and error logs. Per-account and per-key usage stay.
confirmResetBody: Request history and error logs are deleted. Per-account and per-key usage stay. This cannot be undone.
twoFactor.title: Two-factor sign-in
twoFactor.hint: Ask for a code from an authenticator app after the admin password.
twoFactor.offHint: Sign-in asks only for the password. Turn this on to also ask for a 6-digit code from an app such as Google Authenticator, 1Password or Aegis.
twoFactor.onHint: Sign-in asks for a code from your authenticator app after the password.
twoFactor.onSince: On since {time}. Sign-in asks for a code after the password.
twoFactor.codesLeft_one: {count} unused code left. Each code signs in once without the app.
twoFactor.codesLeft_other: {count} unused codes left. Each code signs in once without the app.
twoFactor.codesLow: You are almost out of recovery codes. Make new ones while you can still sign in.
twoFactor.resetByEnv: ADMIN_RESET_2FA is set on the server, so each start turns two-factor sign-in off. Remove it to turn this on.
twoFactor.lockoutNote: Lost the app and the recovery codes? Start the server once with {env} to turn two-factor sign-in off.
twoFactor.codeWrong: That code is not right. Check that your phone's clock is correct.
twoFactor.codeInvalid: Enter the 6-digit code from the app.
twoFactor.setupHint: Scan the QR code with your authenticator app, or type the secret into it. Then enter the code it shows.
twoFactor.qrAlt: QR code for your authenticator app
twoFactor.secretHint: Cannot scan? Type this secret into the app:
twoFactor.accountName: It shows up in the app as {issuer} (admin).
twoFactor.enabled: Two-factor sign-in is on. Other signed-in sessions were ended.
twoFactor.codesHint: If you lose your phone, each code signs in once in place of a code from the app.
twoFactor.codesOnce: These codes are shown only now. Keep them somewhere safe, such as a password manager.
twoFactor.disableHint: Sign-in will ask only for the password. Confirm with a current code.
twoFactor.newCodesHint: The old codes stop working. Confirm with a current code.
twoFactor.newCodesDone: The old codes no longer work. Each new code signs in once.
metrics.title: Prometheus metrics
metrics.hint: Expose request, token, credit, account and proxy numbers for Prometheus.
metrics.switchHint: Off by default. Prometheus reads it with the bearer token below.
metrics.more: Counters: requests by status, model, account and API key, tokens, credits and upstream errors by category, plus a latency histogram. Gauges: each account's state and each proxy's health. Counters start from zero when the server starts.
metrics.endpointHint: Point Prometheus at this address, as it reaches this server.
metrics.tokenHint: Prometheus sends it in the Authorization header. Anyone with it can read the numbers.
metrics.regenerateBody: The current token stops working at once. Give Prometheus the new one.
